terms.meaning: A framework built on React that turns code into a working website, including page routing and a build step.
A React setting that makes the development version check for common mistakes and warn about them.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Turning on strict development checks
sections.what: Exports one settings object that switches on React's strict mode. Developers see extra warnings while the site runs locally, and users see no change.
sections.why: Likely reason: to catch bugs early in development. Reason not stated in the code.

summary: A short settings file that tells Next.js, the framework that runs this website, to use its stricter development checks.
purpose: Sets the options Next.js reads when it builds or runs the site. Only one option is set here.
why: Likely reason: turning on strict mode makes React warn about common mistakes during development. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Next.js loads this file when you run the development server or a build. It reads the settings object and applies them. Nothing else in this file runs.
inputs: None from users. It is read by the Next.js tooling when the project starts or builds.
outputs: Changes how the site behaves in development. Strict mode can cause some effects to run twice in development, which is normal.
risks: Few. Removing the setting would hide some React warnings but would not break the site.
debug: If the site behaves oddly in development only, check whether an effect runs twice. Try turning this option off to compare.
